title: Mother’s Wax Museum | Kolkata Trips
description: Plan your visit to Mother's Wax Museum Kolkata with this complete guide covering ticket price, timings, exhibits, best time to visit, nearby attractions
textContent: Mother’s Wax Museum Mother’s Wax Museum is one of Kolkata’s most popular modern attractions, offering visitors the opportunity to see lifelike wax statues of renowned personalities from India and around the world. Located in New Town near Eco Park, it is India’s first wax museum established by a municipal corporation and has become a favorite destination for families, school groups, photographers, and tourists. The museum showcases meticulously crafted wax figures of freedom fighters, scientists, artists, sports personalities, political leaders, film stars, musicians, and fictional characters. Visitors can pose alongside these incredibly realistic sculptures, making it one of the city’s most photogenic attractions. Whether you are exploring New Town or planning a Kolkata city tour, Mother’s Wax Museum provides an entertaining and educational experience suitable for all age groups. Quick Information Information Details Location New Town, Kolkata Established 2014 Managed By New Town Kolkata Development Authority (NKDA) Famous For Life-size wax statues of famous personalities Ideal Visit Duration 1–2 hours Photography Allowed (subject to museum guidelines) History of Mother’s Wax Museum Mother’s Wax Museum was inaugurated in 2014 by the New Town Kolkata Development Authority (NKDA). The museum was named in honor of Mother Teresa, whose humanitarian work left an everlasting impact on Kolkata and the world. It was conceived to provide an affordable, educational, and entertaining attraction comparable to internationally renowned wax museums. Since its opening, the museum has continuously expanded its collection by adding new personalities representing different fields such as science, literature, sports, cinema, politics, music, and social service. Today, it is regarded as one of the most visited attractions in New Town and complements nearby destinations like Eco Park and Biswa Bangla Gate. Architecture and Design The museum occupies a modern multi-storey building designed specifically for exhibition purposes. The interiors feature: Themed galleries Controlled lighting Realistic backgrounds Interactive photo zones Air-conditioned exhibition halls Wide visitor walkways Each wax figure is carefully positioned with props and themed settings that recreate iconic moments from history, cinema, sports, and public life. Ambedkar Swami Vivekananda Mother Teresa Scientists Albert Einstein Sir Isaac Newton A. P. J. Abdul Kalam Jagadish Chandra Bose Sports Legends Sachin Tendulkar M. S. Dhoni Virat Kohli P. V. Why Visit Mother’s Wax Museum? The museum appeals to visitors for several reasons: Exceptionally realistic wax sculptures Excellent photography opportunities Family-friendly atmosphere Educational exhibits Comfortable indoor environment Suitable throughout the year Convenient location near Eco Park Mother’s Wax Museum Timings Day Opening Hours Tuesday – Sunday 12:00 PM – 7:30 PM Monday Closed Timings may change on public holidays or for maintenance. Mother’s Wax Museum Entry Fee Visitor Approximate Ticket Price Adults ₹250 Children ₹150 School Groups Special rates may be available Ticket prices are subject to revision. Check the official website before your visit. Best Time to Visit Mother’s Wax Museum can be visited throughout the year due to its indoor setting. The most pleasant months are: October to March Winter holidays Christmas season Durga Puja vacations Weekday afternoons for fewer crowds Morning and early afternoon visits generally offer a more relaxed experience than weekends and public holidays. How to Reach Mother’s Wax Museum By Metro The nearest metro stations on Kolkata’s East-West Metro provide convenient access, followed by a short taxi or app-cab ride. By Bus Numerous buses connect Esplanade, Salt Lake, Howrah, and other parts of Kolkata to New Town. By Taxi App-based taxis and yellow taxis can easily reach the museum from anywhere in Kolkata. Approximate travel times: Airport: 20–25 minutes Howrah Station: 45–60 minutes Sealdah Station: 35–45 minutes Park Street: 40–50 minutes Nearby Attractions Combine your visit with nearby attractions: Eco Park Biswa Bangla Gate Nazrul Tirtha New Town Coffee House Rabindra Tirtha Japanese Forest at Eco Park Seven Wonders Park (Eco Park) Butterfly Garden (Eco Park) Many visitors explore these attractions together during a full-day visit to New Town. Photography Photography is one of the museum’s biggest attractions. Visitors can: Take selfies with wax figures Capture family photographs Create themed portraits Photograph museum interiors Flash photography or professional equipment may be restricted in certain sections. Visitor Tips Visit on weekdays for fewer crowds. Carry your camera or smartphone fully charged. Wear comfortable walking shoes. Maintain a safe distance from the wax statues unless permitted. Do not touch the exhibits. Purchase tickets in advance during holidays if available. Allocate at least 1–2 hours for a comfortable visit. Combine the visit with Eco Park for a full-day itinerary. Interesting Facts It is India’s first municipal corporation-operated wax museum. The museum is named after Mother Teresa. Several statues are created by skilled Indian artists. New personalities are added periodically. It is among the most popular attractions in New Town. Thousands of tourists and school students visit every year. Frequently Asked Questions (FAQs) 1. Where is Mother’s Wax Museum located? It is located in New Town, Kolkata, close to Eco Park. 2. Why is it called Mother’s Wax Museum? The museum is named in honor of Mother Teresa for her humanitarian contributions to Kolkata. 3. What are the museum timings? It is generally open from 12:00 PM to 7:30 PM, Tuesday to Sunday, and remains closed on Mondays. 4. How much is the entry ticket? The approximate ticket price is ₹250 for adults and ₹150 for children, though prices may change. 5. How long does a visit take? Most visitors spend between 1 and 2 hours exploring the museum. 6. Is photography allowed? Yes, photography is generally permitted, subject to museum rules. 7. Is the museum suitable for children? Yes. It is a family-friendly attraction that is popular with children and school groups. 8. Which celebrities can I see inside? The museum features figures of national leaders, scientists, sports personalities, film stars, musicians, and international icons. 9. Can I visit Eco Park on the same day? Yes. Eco Park is located nearby, making it easy to combine both attractions in a single outing. 10. What is the best season to visit? October to March offers the most comfortable weather for sightseeing in Kolkata, although the museum itself can be visited year-round. 11. Is parking available? Yes, parking facilities are generally available near the museum. 12. Is the museum wheelchair accessible? Most public areas are designed to be accessible, but it is advisable to confirm current accessibility arrangements before visiting. 13. Are food and drinks available inside? Food and beverages are generally not allowed inside the exhibition galleries, though eateries are available nearby. 14. Is it worth visiting? Yes. The museum offers a unique combination of entertainment, education, and excellent photo opportunities, making it one of the top attractions in New Town. 15. Can the museum be included in a Kolkata sightseeing tour? Absolutely. It is often included in customized Kolkata sightseeing itineraries, especially those focusing on New Town and Eco Park.
